messages:
Maya (Head of Strategy): Follow-up thread from the all-hands  drop quick Qs about mission, market focus, or how we should frame competitors. Keep them short.
Tara (Sales): Need a crisp one-liner for sales decks that isn't the same as the website hero. Something more operational.
Asha (CEO): Try: "Redwood gives engineering teams consistent performance controls and cost predictability for LLMs across hosted, reserved, and private deployments."
Ben (Solutions Eng): From field: customers ask what metrics prove “predictable” — what should reps cite?
Marco (CTO): Recommend p50/p95 latency, per-route token cost, cache hit rate, and rollback time. Those are the numbers engineering buyers ask for.
Priya (VP Product): Also add a practical migration trigger for Hosted -> Dedicated: sustained throughput constraints affecting p95 or unit cost; we'll publish a short checklist with example thresholds.
Tara (Sales): Pricing question: are reserved commit discounts going public soon? reps need a standard line.
Asha (CEO): Not public yet. We're running invite-only pilots for commit discounts and SLA bundles this quarter. Share conservative guidance only.
Ben (Solutions Eng): For Private deployments: sales want an honest time-to-onboard estimate to set expectations. Can we give a range?
Marco (CTO): Say: typical Private onboarding 4-8 weeks depending on custom kernel tuning, quantization validation, and customer network setup. Hosted is immediate; Dedicated is usually 1-2 weeks.
Maya (Head of Strategy): How do we talk about competitors without naming them? Marketing needs a short paragraph.
Asha (CEO): Focus on outcomes: emphasize cost controls, consistent runtime across environments, and canary-driven rollouts that reduce regression risk. Avoid naming vendors.
Priya (VP Product): Example paragraph: "Instead of only exposing models, Redwood ships a runtime and operations experience so teams can deliver LLM features with predictable latency, measurable unit cost, and safe rollouts across any deployment mode."
Tara (Sales): Any guidance on when to suggest Private vs Dedicated for prospects worried about compliance?
Ben (Solutions Eng): Short rule: If policy requires customer-managed networking or on-prem data handling, propose Private. If the ask is dedicated capacity and stronger isolation but not network control, propose Dedicated.
Maya (Head of Strategy): Leadership asks product teams to prioritize features based on 3 signals: customer blockers for revenue, measurable cost/latency impact, and operational risk that affects rollouts.
Marco (CTO): Tech nuance to add: some infra features (e.g., L2 cache) can give big cost wins for caching-heavy workloads; flag those by expected unit-cost delta in planning docs.
Tara (Sales): Competitor question from AE: Can reps say we replace cloud endpoints?
Asha (CEO): Publicly say we "complement or replace depending on customer needs". Internally we keep a competitor playbook with direct comparisons for deal teams.
ops-bot: Recording + slides uploaded: https://redwood.example.com/all-hands/2281234567 :white_check_mark:
Maya (Head of Strategy): I'll compile a 1-page exec summary, a 5-bullet sales FAQ, and the Hosted->Dedicated checklist. Will post drafts by Friday. Thanks all.
Tara (Sales): Perfect  will review and add field examples.
Ben (Solutions Eng): I'll add onboarding caveats for Private to the doc draft.
Asha (CEO): Thanks everyone. Closing the thread EOD unless new issues surface.
